title: Film Federation of India Opens Submissions for India's 99th Academy Awards Entry
excerpt: The FFI has begun accepting films for consideration as India's official Oscar entry, with new Academy rules allowing festival-winning films to qualify independently for the first time.
body:
• The Film Federation of India has opened submissions for India's official entry to the 99th Academy Awards in the Best International Feature Film category
  • New Academy rules allow films winning top prizes at Cannes, Venice, Toronto, and other major festivals to qualify independently, bypassing national selection committees
  • The Academy's deadline for International Feature Film submissions is September 30, 2026, with the ceremony set for March 2027
  • India's most recent entry, Neeraj Ghaywan's Homebound, was shortlisted among 15 films for the 98th Academy Awards earlier this year

The Film Federation of India has opened the application process for filmmakers to submit their work for consideration as India's official entry to the 99th Academy Awards. The announcement, made this week by FFI president Firdausul Hasan, kicks off what has become one of Indian cinema's most closely watched annual selection cycles.

The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled for March 2027, with the Academy's submission deadline for the International Feature Film category set for September 30, 2026. Films eligible for consideration must have their first theatrical release between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026, with a minimum one-week theatrical run.

New Rules Change the Landscape

This year's process unfolds under significantly revised Academy rules that could reshape how Indian films compete for the Oscar. Under the new guidelines, films that win top honors at major international festivals — including Cannes, Venice, Berlin, Toronto, Sundance, and Busan — can now qualify directly for the International Feature Film category without being selected as their country's official entry.

The change is significant for India, where the FFI's selection process has periodically drawn criticism. In 2013, Ritesh Batra's The Lunchbox, which premiered at Cannes to wide acclaim, was passed over in favor of The Good Road — a decision that sparked public debate about the selection committee's criteria and led filmmaker Anurag Kashyap to publicly question the process.

"If these rules had been implemented earlier, a film like Payal Kapadia's All We Imagine as Light could have been included in the Oscar race even without becoming India's official entry."

— Academy Awards analysis

Under the updated framework, the credit for the International Feature Film award will also shift from the submitting country to the film's director — a change that acknowledges individual artistic achievement over national representation.

Building on Homebound's Run

India enters this cycle with fresh momentum from the 98th Academy Awards, where Neeraj Ghaywan's Homebound was selected as India's official entry and went on to be shortlisted among 15 films from 86 countries. The film, starring Ishaan Khatter, Vishal Jethwa, and Janhvi Kapoor, premiered at Cannes' Un Certain Regard section and had executive producer Martin Scorsese attached to the project.

While Homebound did not ultimately receive a nomination, its shortlisting represented India's strongest Oscar showing in recent years. India has been nominated for the Best International Feature Film award three times in its history, beginning with Mother India in 1958 and most recently with Lagaan in 2002.

The Selection Process

The FFI, which has managed India's Oscar submissions since 1957, assembles a jury of industry professionals — directors, producers, writers, editors, and journalists — to evaluate submitted films. The selection committee typically comprises members who are National Award winners, and the process involves screenings of all eligible entries before a final vote.

In past cycles, the FFI has required that submitted films embody "Indianness," with at least 60% of dialogue in an Indian language and approximately 90% of shooting completed within India. The final selection is typically announced in late September.

What's Next for Diaspora Cinema Fans

For Indian diaspora audiences who follow the Oscar race closely, this year's submission cycle carries added weight. The new festival-bypass rule means that Indian films gaining international recognition at European and North American festivals may have multiple paths to Oscar contention, creating a richer field of contenders than in previous years.

The FFI's selection is expected to be announced before the Academy's September 30 deadline, with the shortlist for Best International Feature Film typically revealed in December.
